To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
synchronous programming is applicable to system programming, but that the current state of the art of synchronous languages is not adequate to the task.

1) the synchronous programming paradigm is a viable approach to system software development, and that 2) Esterel and RC can be successfully applied to the development of system software, but that 3) the soft‐instruction approach is more promising for system software, especially for real‐time system software, and that 4) a soft‐instruction language is needed to realize the potential benefits of the soft‐instruction architecture.
synchronous/reactive languages can be used to develop concurrent system software.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a methodology for the construction of concurrent system software, and the design of a programming language to support that methodology.
the application of the reactive paradigm to system software development.
the development of a methodology for the design and implementation of concurrent system software.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the applicability of synchronous programming to system software development is limited.

synchronous languages are not suitable for general system programming, but they are suitable for certain system programming tasks and are especially suitable for the development of embedded systems and real‐time applications.
imperative synchronous/reactive programming languages are a viable alternative to traditional imperative sequential languages for system software development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

synchronous languages are not suitable for the development of concurrent system software, although they may be used in the design of some components, particularly in real‐time and embedded systems, where the environment can be assumed to be well‐defined.
synchronous languages are well suited to the development of concurrent system software.
the use of synchronous/reactive languages is an excellent choice for system programming.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of synchronous languages for system programming is feasible.
imperative synchronous languages are a good fit for system programming.

the design of a synchronous language is not a matter of choosing a set of primitives and rules for combining them, but a question of choosing a suitable semantic model and of designing an implementation that respects it.
